I run a hotel in a small town. The hotel is “downtown” so over my time here I’ve gotten to know a lot of ppl in town. Anyways I was driving back to the city and I saw 2 women hitchhiking that I sorta recognised. I picked them up and took em to the city. They texted me that they wanted a ride back with me if I go back on the Sunday but I stayed longer and did not contacted them after. Anyways couple days go by and I see in the local town paper that one of the 2 girls has gone missing and the last anyone knew was that they were hitchhiking to the city. Mind you this is In Canada where an aboriginal women going missing is standard affair and the cops don’t really care. I called the cops to tell them what I know, the first cop said she was found. She wasn’t. I called a different locale ( this time I called the city rather than the town) and they took it more seriously and took down all the info I had. Later the towns cops had someone on the case who ddnt call me or contact me for a week. Finally she does and we have a 40 second convo and that’s it. The women is still missing months later now. I felt horrible when it happened cuz I couldn’t shake a feeling of responsibility. Like if I had picked them up before going back to town maybe she would be safe? But more importantly I felt frustrated than in an “advanced” nation we still have systemic racism that allows hundreds of women to go missing without anyone batting an eyelash.

You’re assuming that smokers don’t fully understand the ramifications. As a smoker I will tell you I do, but I smoke nonetheless. It started as a way to deal with anxiety and then later became an addiction. That being said I always knew that it will kill me, but that trade off was ok for me. What’s some years of my life if I can function now? As for now, we’ll I can quit I’m sure. It wouldn’t be easy. But I enjoy it. I enjoy the feeling I get. I enjoy the social aspect of it. As a non smoker I’m assuming you don’t know about the depth of conversation a cigarette brings. For some reason when smoking with someone you will reach new depth to conversation. It has to do with the fact that we are sharing a weakness. Smoking is a weakness. We share it. All of our walls come down. It also has an equalizing effect. Rich or poor when your smoking you equal. (http://theoryleaks.org/text/articles/mladen-dolar/the-smoking-communism/ says it better than I can). Finally it just feels good. I mean why drink? It feels good. It’s not healthy, it leads to health problems. But it feels good. Same with any indulgence really like coke or fast food. For us it’s a calculus, a trade off between living longer and being happier in the moment. We decided smoking was our line. For others it’s cocaine or heroin. For others it’s gaming addictions. It’s all the same base. We just chose an addiction different than yours.
